free_tier.stated: Historical: a free link protector whose API took a username and password and returned a folder URL. 'URL: http://linksave.in/protect?api=[username]:[Password]' with fields for links, mirrors, captcha on/off and container types rsdf/ccf/dlc. Nothing of the service answers today.
free_tier.notes: The 2011 API description is third-party. No current page on the domain exists to confirm or price anything.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: it held links, not bytes.

retention.stated: unknown and now moot: the service is unreachable, so nothing is retained.

interface_detail: Historical HTTP API only: POST to /protect?api=user:pass with *save, *links and optional container/captcha fields. Today the domain issues a 302 to a wildcard host that does not resolve in DNS.
tooling: JDownloader used to ship a linksave decrypter plugin. Nothing to drive now.
chaining: none: a dead container service removes an indirection layer, it does not add one.

limits.value: no service: the wildcard host ww17.linksave.in fails name resolution

limits_note: The 302 target is the same wildcard pattern that linkcrypt.ws now uses, which suggests one operator or one parking setup for both domains.
binding_note: Nothing binds because nothing answers: at any volume the first failure is DNS.

identity_cost.detail: Historical API used a username:password pair embedded in the URL; whether registration was open is not verifiable now.

reliability_note: Dead as of today: 302 to ww17.linksave.in, then getaddrinfo failure (errno 11004). Last known live capture is the Wayback snapshot of 2025-05-24, HTTP 200.
confidence_note: The description of what it was rests on a 2011 forum post and the archive capture, and is marked reported.

evidence.proved: HTTP 302 to https://ww17.linksave.in/, then 'getaddrinfo failed' errno 11004; 0 bytes; no hash
the sibling domain fails identically: 302 to https://ww17.linkcrypt.ws/, then DNS failure
Wayback capture 2025-05-24 06:39:44 of the root: HTTP 200, text/html, 1122 bytes recorded
reported, 2011: the protect API signature and the rsdf/ccf/dlc container options

notes: linkcrypt.ws is the same case and is recorded here rather than as a second file: both 302 to the identical ww17.<domain> wildcard and both fail DNS. one dead service with two domains is one fact.
